_note: How a figure holds a gun (src/game/hold.ts, src/game/mannequin.ts). The animation library is a pistol library: it has no rifle clips, so a long gun is not held by the clips at all. It is hung off the chest and both arms are reached onto it, which means every number about where it hangs is one of ours and belongs here rather than buried in the code. The old ones put the grip five centimetres INWARD of the shoulder, and since a rifle's stock is behind its grip, the stock ended up beside the neck and through the chest, which is what the owner saw. A stock belongs in the shoulder pocket, which is outboard of the neck, and a gun long enough to reach past that has to sit further forward.

hold._out: how far outboard of the shoulder joint the grip sits, metres: the shoulder pocket, not the collarbone
hold._drop: how far below the shoulder joint the grip sits, metres
hold._forward: how far in front of the shoulder the grip sits at rest, metres, before any gun that needs more
hold._stockAllow: how far behind the shoulder joint a stock may sit, metres. A stock IS in the shoulder, and the gun hangs outboard of the joint where the torso is not, so the butt passes BESIDE the chest rather than through it: this is what lets it be 18 cm and not zero. Past it the gun is pushed forward until it clears, which is why a sniper stands with its hands further out than an SMG.
hold._maxForward: and how far forward that pushing may ever go, metres: past this the support hand cannot reach the handguard, and a hand that cannot reach its hold is the floating hand

lower._note: the long gun lowered and canted across the body for a sprint or a swap

reach._note: how fast a hand takes its hold and lets go, per second: the grip is quicker than the support hand, because a gun coming up is gripped before it is steadied

_athleticJump: Horizontal speed, m/s, above which a figure in the air plays the athletic jump (the free library's NinjaJump_Idle_Loop, legs tucked) instead of the plain one. Sprint is 6.6 m/s (260 hu/s), so this is faster than a sprint: a slide jump, a pad, a hop chain, not a jump from a standing start or a walk.
_doubleJump: A double jump seen on a figure: its knees come up and go back down as it jumps again, over `time` seconds, the thighs raised `raise` degrees and the knees bent `bend` more at the top, eased (up then down), the body upright. The owner, 2026-09-30, first "there should be an animation for when we double jump for sure", then, of the front flip it first was: "I don't like the flip for double jump. People will double jump all the time and that's hard to hit I assume. Can we just have the legs raise a bit at the same time as the double jump, so there's something there?" SpeedKills' double jump rises for 0.39 s (movement.speedkills.json: sqrt(2 x 52 / 690)), so the knees are down again before its top. A figure first seen with a count of them does not lift for it. Ours.
_wallRun: A wall run seen on a figure (Milestone 604; until then it was the plain jump pose floating beside the wall). EMPULSE's and Titanfall's runners lean off the wall with their feet on it, so the whole figure is turned about the way it runs, round its hips (the pelvis bone's height in the bind pose, measured as each figure is made), by the angle that puts a foot under the hips onto the wall: the player's middle is held the hull's radius off it (movement.json radius, 16 hu, 0.41 m), so asin(0.41 / hip height): the soldier's hips are 0.951 m up, 25.3 degrees. Eased in and out at `rate` a second. Its legs run the run's clip, no faster than `mostRate` times the clip's own pace: a wall run is twice a sprint's speed, and the sprint's legs at double time read as a scramble. The gun stays up, not in the sprint's low carry: a runner on a wall is a runner who can shoot. Ours.
_landing: A landing taken in the legs (mannequin.ts, Milestone 611): the knees give and the body sinks onto them for a moment, as much as the fall was long (dummy.ts land: 0.35 for a hop to 1 for a fall of 0.7 s or more, gone in a quarter of a second), the thighs coming forward `raise` degrees, the knees bending `bend` and the chest leaning `lean` over them at its hardest, the body lowered by what that lifts the feet, so they stay on the ground. Before, only a landing standing still showed one (the library's Jump_Land clip, which this leaves to it), and a player landing on the run from a roof ran straight on as if from the floor. Ours.
_death: A figure's death falls away from the shot that killed it (dummy.ts faceTheShot, Milestone 610). Its fall, the death clip's (the library's Death01 falls backward: the head ends 1.2 m behind where it stood, 0.2 m up) and its hit volumes' topple alike, is backward, and it fell backward whichever way it faced, so a player shot from behind fell onto the shooter; Apex's fall away from the hit. As it goes down it turns its front to where the last hit landed, if that was within `hitFor` seconds and more than `near` metres off its middle across the ground (a hit's point is on the near side, the shooter's), the shortest way round at `turnRate` a second (its fall takes 0.32 s). Knocked with no hit on this page (another page's shot) it falls as it faces. Ours. And never through a wall (Milestone 619): with its back to one it lay through it, every one of 25 such falls at the Neon City's eye-level spots (node_modules/.scratch/deathwall.mts). The way it falls is turned `roomStep` degrees at a time, either way, to the nearest with `room` m clear behind it `roomUp` m over the floor (the head ends 1.2 m behind), or the one with the most room if none has it.
_bank: A runner seen leaning into a turn (mannequin.ts leanIntoTurn, Milestone 609): Apex's and Titanfall's do, and ours ran a curve bolt upright. On the ground above `minSpeed` m/s (a jog), the body leans toward the turn's middle round its feet, as far as a body balanced against the game's gravity would (the angle whose tangent is the sideways acceleration over gravity, movement.json), `share` of that, never more than `most` degrees, eased at `rate` a second; its way of moving and the change in it are read off where the figure goes, smoothed at `smooth` a second (an enemy's position comes in 20 to 30 times a second). Balanced in full, SpeedKills' sprint (14 m/s) turned a radian a second against its gravity (17.5 m/s/s) leans 39 degrees, a cyclist's lean; a third of it, capped at 12, reads as a runner's, and half that turn leans 8. Ours.
_plunge: SLAM's way down seen on a figure (mannequin.ts, Milestone 608): it comes down at 38 m/s (hacks.json slam.downSpeed), faster than anything else in the air stance falls (the skydive's dive is 30 m/s, in its own stance), and it was the jump pose dropping like a stone. Falling faster than `fall` m/s (measured off where the figure's group goes, so an enemy's from its samples), the thighs come up `raise` degrees, the knees bend `bend` more and the chest leans `lean` forward over them, eased at `rate` a second: a body coming down onto what it hits, as Hyper Scape's slam reads. Ours.
_grapple: GRAPPLE seen on a figure (mannequin.ts reachArm, Milestone 607): EMPULSE's and Pathfinder's grapples are an arm thrown at the point and the body hauled after it, and ours was a jump pose with a line drawn from it. While a player's grapple pulls them (hacks.json grapple: until they are within `arrive` of its hook point or `maxSeconds` are up), their left hand lets go of the gun and the arm points at the point, eased in and out at `rate` a second. Ours.
_zipline: A zip line seen on a figure (mannequin.ts ropeAt and reachArm, Milestone 616): Apex's legends ride theirs hanging from the rope by one hand, the gun in the other, and ours stood in the air under the rope with the gun in both hands (the rail clip). Now the left hand lets go of the gun and the arm goes up to the rope, eased in and out at `rate` a second, the hand closed round it, the legs hanging under it (the standing clip's, the thighs `thigh` degrees forward and the knees bent `knee` back) and the gun in the right hand. The rope runs movement.json ziplineHang (2.13 m) over the rider's feet (player.ts hangAt); the hand holds it `grip` [left, under, ahead] m off the point right over the feet. From the soldier's shoulder there its straight arm falls 9 cm short of the rope, so the body is raised until it reaches, `lift` m at most: hung from its hand, its feet a little over the ones the game moves.
_ghost: A squad mate's ghost as the squad sees it (src/game/ghostfigure.ts, Milestone 605): out with a squad mate standing, a player goes on as a ghost, and Hyper Scape's squads see theirs (its echoes) as the players still, a figure of light that runs where they run. Ours was a pale capsule. It is their soldier now, playing its clips from what they send, flat light in their squad colour `opacity` see-through (the capsule's 0.35, a little more for a body's thinner limbs), closing on where they were last heard at `follow` a second (their state arrives 20 to 30 times a second: unsmoothed it stepped). No gun, no shadow, no hit volumes, and only a squad mate's page makes one. Ours.
_spectateCam: Watching someone in third person once you are out (src/game/tpcam.ts, Milestone 615): the camera `back` m behind them and `up` m over their feet, looking at a point `lookAhead` m in front of them and `lookUp` m up (the numbers it always had). It looks out to that place from their head (`pivotUp` m over their feet) first and stops `gap` m short of the first wall on the way, as your own third-person camera stops 0.15 m short of the wall behind you: put there whatever stood there, in the Neon City it was inside the wall behind them or past it.
_selfFade: Your own soldier in third person thinned out as a wall at your back brings the camera in (tpcam.ts selfFadeAt, Milestone 615): whole while the camera is `from` m or more from your eye, gone at `to` m, eased between. The camera stands 2.44 m from the eye at the hip (the e2e reads 2.443), 1.57 m aimed in (0.9 m nearer) and 3 m in front in an emote, so none of those thins it; a wall pulls it to 0.52 m, where the head and shoulders covered a third of the screen (five of the Neon City's eye-level review spots, measured by node_modules/.scratch/tpcam-walls.mts).
_skydive: The battle royale's skydive seen on a figure (Milestone 604; until then the jump pose for the whole fall). Apex's legends fall in two poses, a belly-down glide with the arms out and a head-first dive with the arms back, and which one says where they are going; ours steer the same way (squad.json dive: a level look glides, a look down dives), so the figure is `glide` degrees forward of upright looking level and `dive` looking straight down, as far between as the look is, turned round the hips. The limbs, degrees on the body at rest (the arms as an emote's: raise sideways from hanging, forward from hanging; elbow bent toward the head; arch the back; head back from the chest; thigh back; spread apart; knee bent): gliding, the box a skydiver flies, upper arms out a little past level, forearms up past the head, the back arched, the head up to see ahead, thighs back and apart, shins up behind; diving, the arms at the sides a little out from the body and the legs together, nearly straight (swung back along it, the right arm went 13 to 52 mm into the gun slung on the back). The forearms and shins flutter `flutter[0]` degrees at `flutter[1]` a second. Eased in at `rateIn` a second off the ship and out at `rateOut`: the last `flare` seconds of the fall, at the speed it falls (player.ts figureStance), it is upright, feet first, as Apex's legends take their landing position some 30 m up, and the landing's crouch takes it at the ground (mannequin.ts landUntil). Laid on the air to the last, it turned upright in the landing's first frame; 0.8 s is 10 m over the ground gliding and 24 m diving. The hands are empty for the fall and a long gun is slung on the back, as Apex's legends carry theirs (mannequin.ts holsterMount, Milestone 612): diagonal, the muzzle up over the left shoulder `holster.tilt` degrees off the spine, its grip and magazine toward the left hip, its side flat to the back `holster.gap` m off the skin there, `holster.height` of the way from the lower chest to the neck; the skin is measured off the posed soldier (the furthest-back vertex within `holster.band` m of the spine, its pack and armour with it). At 35 degrees, with its grip toward the right shoulder, the dive's right arm went into the short guns; at 20 with the grip toward the hip and the arms at the sides, no bone is in any of the eight long guns. A pistol is put away. Ours, posed by eye against Apex's.
_sling: A long gun on the back standing, while an emote, an interact, a throw (Milestone 617) or a climb or mantle (618) has the hands (mannequin.ts holsterMount): it vanished and came back, so an enemy dancing or looting showed no gun. As the skydive's holster (its gap and band), but `tilt` degrees off upright and its middle `height` of the way from the lower chest to the neck, measured on the soldier in its bind pose (upright and untwisted) and kept in the chest's frame. Searched through every emote and an interact on every long gun (node_modules/.scratch/slingprobe.mts, how deep the soldier goes into the gun): at the skydive's 20 and 0.3 the right forearm went 43 mm into BOOG's lower end; at 5 and 0.38, nothing of the soldier is in any of the eight guns in any of them.
_slide: A slide seen on a figure (mannequin.ts, Milestone 831): the clip played whole laid the soldier on its back, the gun 25 to 55 degrees off where it looked, and a player shoots sliding (Apex's legends slide sat up, the gun on the aim). Now the slide's legs and hips are played and the gun held on top: the chest brought up through the spine to `back` degrees behind upright (negative is forward: as it stands, 5 forward), and turned round by however far the slide's hips face from `hipsTurn` degrees, the standing clip's (the slide's face 18 the other way, and the rifleman's stance, which turns the chest from the hips, left the stock in the right collarbone); the gun brought up toward the eye at least `ads` of the way, all of it (at the hip on the seated lap PANDA's went 12 cm into the thighs, DEVINOS's tube carried low 10 cm into the chest, and at 0.7 the tube was against the head). Measured on every gun (node_modules/.scratch/slideprobe.mts): the gun under a degree off the look and no deeper in the soldier than standing aimed in, 26 mm at most.
_flatFeet: Standing or crouched still, the soldier's clips hold its toes 16.1 degrees up from its bind pose, so it stood on its heels (measured by apex-lobby for the battle royale's card, Milestone 416: the foot-to-ball line 30.5 degrees down against 46.6 bound, the ankle 0.152 m up and the ball 0.072; the owner asked it fixed). Under `under` m/s each foot is turned back until its toe is no higher than the bind pose has it, eased in and out at `rate` a second (rifle-hold soldiers only; the legacy figures keep their clips). A foot the clips point down (a crouch's kneeling foot) and every moving foot are the clips' own: walking and running, the planted feet come down flat by themselves (measured: 2 to 8 degrees at mid stance). Turned flat, a standing sole was 11 to 22 mm into the floor (its heel had been 44 mm in, the toe 9 above): the standing clip holds the legs lower than a walk's planted foot (the ankle 0.152 m up against 0.174), so a figure standing still is also lifted `lift` m, eased the same way (measured off the boots' lowest skin; not crouched, whose kneeling foot is already above the floor).
_headUp: The soldier's head held up to where it looks (the owner, 2026-10-04: from behind "their head is all tucked down, like chin is to the player's chest, making a headshot from the boog in the back almost impossible"). The clips carry the head down with the chest: measured, the head's middle 43 degrees forward of the neck standing, 52 to 56 aimed, 74 to 80 crouched or sprinting, and from 30 m behind at a standing eye a shot at the back of the head it showed was a headshot 66 times in 100 standing, 40 to 60 aimed and 2 to 7 crouched or sprinting (the neck's and the torso's volumes took the rest). Each frame the Head bone is turned about the figure's left so the face looks at the look's pitch, level when not aiming, `hold` of the way, never more than `most` degrees; before the deliberate tilts on top (a flinch, the aimed nod, the rifle rig's cheek on the stock). Not in an emote or dead.
_headVolume: The soldier's head as it is hit (dummy.ts followBones; the owner, 2026-10-11: "i want to always be able to clearly snipe hs someone from the back"): the smallest ellipsoid that holds every point of the drawn head, a hat with it (mannequin.ts headShape, Khachiyan's method; one fit a kit), turned with its Head bone, and `margin` metres more: VANGUARD's half sizes 0.165, 0.132 and 0.105 with its hat, RUNNER's 0.146, 0.118 and 0.101. A box round the points grown until it held them all was a third again as big, and a shot beside the head took it. The sphere before it, 0.13 m round a middle a hat pulled up, left the bottom of the back of the head outside it: from 30 m behind a shot there went through to the neck's volume, 21 to 34 of every 100 shots at the head a standing soldier showed.
_neckTop: The neck's volume at its top and its foot, metres round (dummy.ts): the drawn neck's thinnest under the skull, measured in the bind pose 0.060 to 0.064 (the neck skin, 1 to 3 cm under the Head bone), and at its foot 0.058 to 0.060 (2 cm under the neck bone; the suit's collar, 0.09 round, lowered there to clear the head). At 0.07 and 0.09 it stood out of the neck at both, and from 30 degrees behind a shot at the bottom of the side of the head took the neck, 5 to 9 of every 100; so its top is 0.03 round, the head's ellipsoid reaching down over the rest, and it stops where the neck's line goes into the head's. Widened again to 0.055 under the head's seam (headSeam), it took 10 to 15 of every 100 points at the bottom of the head from 30 degrees behind, crouched and aimed, past the seam, and a drawn neck shot straight at missed 10 in 100 sprinting where it missed 12.
_torsoTop: The torso's volume's top following the shoulders down (dummy.ts torsoVolume; the soldier's is its chest, the volume's top half, from spine_02 along the upper chest): `[out, down]` pairs, metres out from the middle and how far under the box's flat top (1 cm under the neck bone) it comes there. The drawn top, measured in the bind pose with the collar lowered (over or under the neck bone): +0.012 at 6 cm out, -0.017 at 8, -0.026 at 10, -0.033 at 12, -0.048 at 16, -0.058 at 20, -0.065 at 24; the profile 5 mm inside it. Flat to the edge, the box stood up to 5.5 cm over the shoulders, and from 30 degrees behind a shot at the bottom of the side of the head took the torso, 25 of every 100 there. Then lowered 1 to 1.4 cm more from 8 to 16 cm out: in a pose the shoulders drop from the bind pose (measured over 13 poses, the drawn top 10 to 16 cm out as low as 0.228 to 0.268 over the chest's middle where the profile stood at 0.287 to 0.294), and RUNNER aiming 30 degrees down, its bare right shoulder under it, the chest took 5 of every 280 shots at the skull from straight behind, 9 to 12 cm short of the head. A drawn torso shot straight at goes into no volume 1 to 1.5 in 100 more often for it.
_torsoBack: And front to back (dummy.ts torsoVolume): `[along, down]` pairs, metres forward of the box's middle (+ toward the chest; the box is 0.32 deep, its middle 8 mm in front of the neck's line) and how far under its flat top it comes there. The drawn top near the middle, measured as torsoTop: -0.051 to -0.057 under the neck bone behind the neck (the collar lowered), +0.005 at the neck, +0.012 to +0.017 at the collar's front, then -0.038, -0.055 and -0.067 down the chest 12, 14 and 16 cm in front; 5 mm inside it. Flat to the back, the box stood 4.5 cm out of the upper back behind the neck, and from 30 degrees behind a shot at the bottom of the head went in through its back.
_neckBelow: How far under the neck bone the neck's volume reaches down (dummy.ts followBones), metres: to the torso's top behind the neck (5.6 cm under it, torsoBack), so a shot at the back of the neck's base has a volume to hit.
_armVolume: The soldier's arms as they are hit (dummy.ts followBones): each arm two cylinders round its bones, the upper arm from the shoulder to the elbow (`upper`: its radius at the shoulder and at the elbow, metres), the forearm from the elbow to `hand` metres past the wrist (`fore`, the same), so the hand is in it. Measured round the bones, standing with BOOG (tools: the skin weighted half and more to each segment's bones): the upper arm 0.26 long, 95 in 100 of its skin within 0.126 of the bone over its first fifth (VANGUARD's shoulder armour; RUNNER's bare 0.097 to 0.126) and 0.080 to 0.081 over its last (the upper arm's radius at the shoulder set under that, 0.09: at 0.11 its end stood over RUNNER's bare shoulder raised aiming down, and from straight behind took 5 of every 280 shots at the skull; the arms' fit to the drawn arms the same at both); the forearm 0.268 long, 0.073 to 0.076 at the elbow, 0.058 to 0.062 at the wrist; the closed hand 0.076 to 0.085 past the wrist at its middle, 0.13 at the fingertips. One 0.6 m box a whole arm, shoulder to hand, stood half its length past a bent arm's shoulder, behind it and beside the head: from 30 degrees behind a soldier aiming DEVINOS down, a shot at the head it showed went into it, 135 of every 468.
_legVolume: The soldier's legs as they are hit (dummy.ts followBones), zone legs: each a cylinder round the thigh from the hip to the knee (`thigh`, its radius at each end, metres) and one round the calf from the knee to the ankle (`calf`), and a box round the boot (`foot`: `size` across, up and along the sole, `mid` its middle from the ankle bone, up the calf and along the sole). Measured round the bones standing with BOOG (the skin weighted half and more to each segment's bones, 95 in 100 of it within): the thigh 0.39 long, 0.159 to 0.165 of the bone at the hip (VANGUARD's holsters; RUNNER's 0.138 to 0.145), 0.109 to 0.114 at the knee; the calf 0.388, 0.12 at the knee, 0.13 over the boot's top, 0.104 at the ankle; the boot, 98 in 100 of it, from 0.074 to 0.102 behind the ankle to 0.26 to 0.29 in front, 0.17 to 0.19 under it, 0.07 to 0.10 either side. One box 0.42 across, 0.92 long and 0.3 deep from the pelvis to the feet stood in the air between the legs and missed the leg a stride swung out of it: shots at a drawn leg that went into a volume within 6 cm of it, 9 to 23 in 100 (standing, walking, sprinting, crouched, jumping, sliding), and 58 to 80 in 100 into none.
_handVolume: Each of the soldier's hands as it is hit (dummy.ts followBones), zone body: a sphere `r` metres round, its middle `at` of the way from the hand bone to the middle finger's second joint, so it follows the fingers as they close round each gun. Measured holding BOOG, USSO, APUHTHEE, DEVINOS and CHOOCH, at the hip and aimed: 95 in 100 of the hand's skin (weighted half and more to the hand or a finger) within 0.077 to 0.086 of that middle (0.083 to 0.105 a quarter of the way along, 0.092 to 0.112 three quarters). With none, a shot at a hand went through it into nothing 22 to 26 times in 100 of the shots at an arm, most at the left hand's fingers round the fore-end. Not VANGUARD's shoulder armour, half of whose shots go past the upper arm's cylinder: a sphere round it (0.117 m, 90 in 100 of its skin) is mostly air round a curved plate, and from 30 degrees behind it took 88 to 98 of every 500 shots at the head the soldier showed, aiming. A box fitted to the plate itself (along its own axes, 22 by 19 by 9 cm) was no better: shots at the arms within 6 cm went from 60 to 64 in 100 and none fewer into nothing (the misses are the left hand's fingertips), while 12 of VANGUARD's 39 states lost head shots from behind to it, to 70 in 100 with DEVINOS aimed down.
_dressPerFrame: How many figures put the soldier on in one frame, at most (dummy.ts dress). Every figure is its hit volumes until then; the range's ten are made with the page, before the soldier is in, and the courses' fifty pop-ups all at once, and a soldier made for each in the same frame would stall it. Ours: two a frame dresses the range in five frames and a room of pop-ups as they rise.
_headSeam: How far past a body volume's way in a shot may go on into the same figure's head volume and take the head, metres (hitpick.ts). Measured from 30 m behind and 30 degrees off, standing to crouched and aimed: of the shots at the head it showed that went into the neck's or the chest's volume first, the head's was 6 to 56 mm on through the neck's (a quarter of them within 16, half within 20, nine in ten within 33) and 0 to 99 through the chest's (half within 26, nine in ten within 59). All of them at the head's lowest 6 cm, the jaw and the nape, which the neck and the collar meet.
_chestUp: The soldier's chest held no more than `most` degrees forward of upright, measured along the upper chest (spine_03 to the neck, what stands between a shooter behind and the head) in the figure's frame, the rest taken back through spine_02 and spine_03 before the look's own bend (the owner, 2026-10-04, choosing it: the clips lean the chest 33 to 40 degrees crouched and aimed or sprinting, and from behind the shoulder armour and the pack hid much of the head even held up, headUp). A lean back, a slide's, is the clip's. Not in an emote or dead. At 20, crouched and aimed the raised right shoulder (VANGUARD's shoulder armour, RUNNER's suit) hid 12 to 22 of every 100 points of the skull from 30 m behind, straight or 30 degrees off (2026-10-11, the owner: "i want to always be able to clearly snipe hs someone from the back"); at 12, 0 to 3; at 5, none; at 8, the side views of a crouched aim and a sprint still the clips' own.
_aimBend: How an aimed look's pitch bends the soldier, as shares of it for spine_01, spine_02 and spine_03 (mannequin.ts): looking up, the chest bends back over its two upper bones; looking down, the soldier's own `down` bends it a little at the waist and the head goes down onto the stock for the rest (mannequin.ts holdHeadUp). Bent 0.9 of the look at the chest looking down as up, 30 degrees down put the head down between the shoulders, and from 30 m behind the shoulders, the back armour and the raised right arm hid 56 to 76 of every 100 points of the head turned to a shooter straight behind and 57 to 84 from 30 degrees off (BOOG and APUHTHEE, VANGUARD and RUNNER). Measured at 30 degrees down by how much of the look bends the body: 1.3 hid 62 to 94, 0.9 56 to 84 wherever it bent (the waist, the chest, both), 0.5 30 to 60, 0.3 23 to 46, 0.1 13 to 40 (the skull alone, over the head's lowest 6 cm: 0 to 26). But the hands need the body bent to keep a gun along a look down: looking 35 down, the skfigure hold's bar (a wrist bent 60 degrees at most, the gun 40 mm into the body at most) held every gun bent 0.9 at the chest; bent at the waist, every gun but BIGANTLER, REZ, CHOOCH, STRYDER and DEVINOS at 0.3 (their wrists 62 to 75; DEVINOS 66 come up from its carry), all but CHOOCH at 0.5 (DEVINOS's right wrist on the bar, 60: bent 0.6 or 0.7 to clear it, its raised arm and the chest took 9 to 18 of every 100 shots at RUNNER's head from behind), and CHOOCH (its right wrist 62 at 0.7) at 0.9. So each gun bends as little as its hold allows: `down`, or its own in `downByGun`. Looking up, `up`.
